signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Tension
signals.text: The G10 scorecard records JPY as the week's strongest performer with a 1W average of +1.488% across 7 pairs, while NZD lags at -0.810% across 4 pairs, creating an extreme 2.298% bilateral spread. Escalating US-Iran military strikes and surging crude oil (WTI at $94.50) drive cross-asset defensiveness, accelerating an unwind of high-carry funding pairs despite normal broader equity volatility with VIX at 15.7. A large nominal policy divergence remains in place with RBNZ at 2.75% versus BoJ at 1.0% providing a +175bp carry buffer, yet JPY momentum dominates as BEER fair value tracks NZD/JPY stretched at z=-3.29σ below model equilibrium. Spot trades under heavy distribution alongside NZD speculative net short positioning of -23,004 contracts (pctl 4). Sustained risk aversion keeps downside momentum intact toward key psychological thresholds. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY, thematic cross-asset unwind dominating nominal carry. Catalyst: BoJ rate decision on 18 Sep. Risk: De-escalation headlines in the Middle East reverse the broad yen bid.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Positioning Unwind
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 153.26, sitting well below its SMA20 (158.45) and SMA200 (158.43) cluster after extending weekly losses to -1.54%. CFTC data shows leveraged funds holding an extreme net short JPY position of -111,297 contracts (pctl 2, z -2.18), creating severe short-covering pressure on spot. Derivatives markets aggressively position for deeper downside, with 1M 25d risk reversals displaying a strong put skew of -2.46 alongside an ATM implied volatility of 10.6% versus 30-day realized volatility of 11.3% (VRP -0.7%). Retail sentiment reflects extreme asymmetry with 86% long positioning, directly contradicting the persistent institutional short unwind. Although the Fed-BoJ policy differential of +275bp (Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0%) structurally favors the dollar, spot remains trapped in a liquidation cycle while holding beneath moving average resistance. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, crowded spec short covering superseding carry. Catalyst: US Core PPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Rebound and daily close above the 158.45 SMA20 level.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7234, maintaining an upward trajectory above its SMA20 of 0.7151 and SMA50 of 0.7054. Leveraged funds hold a stretched net long position of +50,250 contracts (pctl 94, z +1.79), representing the upper decile of 52-week positioning even as WoW delta stalled at -3,328 contracts. Retail positioning shows a mirror extreme at 91% short, establishing a stark retail versus institutional positioning divergence. The underlying yield structure remains constructive with RBA at 4.35% versus Fed at 3.75%, providing a +60bp cash rate advantage reinforced by an Australian Economic Surprise Index reading of +17.3. However, with BEER fair value indicating spot is rich at z=+1.78σ and options market 25d RR showing a -0.46 put skew, upside velocity is increasingly constrained by positioning saturation. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD, supported by carry advantage but constrained by crowded longs. Catalyst: US Core PPI today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: A break below technical support at the 0.7151 SMA20.

signals.title: EUR/USD — CB Spread + Pre-ECB Compression
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1643, consolidating slightly above its SMA20 (1.1619) and SMA200 (1.1638) support cluster ahead of immediate policy risk. The structural macro backdrop remains weighed down by central bank policy divergence, where Fed at 3.75% versus ECB at 2.40% generates a 135bp nominal yield spread favoring USD. Leveraged funds hold net short euro exposure of -52,784 contracts (pctl 31, z -0.39), while asset managers sit on +291,129 contracts of net longs, reflecting balanced multi-week institutional positioning. Options markets show contained premium with 1M ATM implied volatility at 5.1% against 4.6% HV30 (VRP +0.5%) and a neutral 25d risk reversal at -0.21. A daily close above the 200-day moving average is required to open technical targets toward 1.1700, but rate differentials restrict aggressive top-side expansion. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD, policy spread limiting upside momentum. Catalyst: ECB Refinancing Rate decision today at 12:15 UTC. Risk: An unexpected 50bp ECB rate hike that forces a rapid compression of the transatlantic yield gap.
